evidence.locator: R1 IN OUT 100k; C1 OUT 0 100n; .meas tran vout_1ms FIND v(OUT) AT=1m
comp ref R1 value 100k; nets /IN (R1.1), /OUT (R1.2, C1.1), GND (C1.2)

decisions.reason: Executable rc_transient check ran successfully (exit 0, 1025 data points) and measured vout_1ms = 0.0951625 V, outside the declared [0.62, 0.65] V limit from fixture requirement 1. The measurement is independently confirmed by closed-form RC theory for the saved values (R1=100k, C1=100n gives tau=10 ms; 1-exp(-0.1)=0.09516 V at 1 ms and 1-exp(-0.5)=0.39347 V at 5 ms match the log exactly), so the deck faithfully represents the native netlist and the failing criterion is genuine. A supported failing executable check must remain accepted; root cause is recorded in accepted finding circuit/CKT-001.

requirement 1: 0.62 V <= V(/OUT, 1 ms) <= 0.65 V; intended R1 = 10 kohm, C1 = 100 nF
line "R1 IN OUT 100k" generated from the native XML netlist

decisions.reason: Established defect and canonical root cause of the rc-step check failure: R1 is populated as 100k in both the native schematic and the board footprint, 10x the intended 10 kohm stated in fixture requirement 1, giving tau = 10 ms instead of 1 ms. The alleged mechanism verifies analytically: V(1 ms) = 1-exp(-0.1) = 0.09516 V matches the measured 9.516251e-02 to all printed digits, and vout_5ms = 0.3934693 matches 1-exp(-0.5), independently confirming tau = 10 ms from two points. The violated limit is the packet's own declared criterion, and the intended 10k value would yield 0.6321 V, inside the window, so blocking severity is supported.

evidence.locator: .meas tran vout_5ms FIND v(OUT) AT=5m (no limits); VSTEP IN 0 PWL(0 0 1n 1)
requirement 1 bounds only the 1 ms point; scope-limits paragraph declares idealized coverage

decisions.reason: Supported informational concern, not a defect. Factually correct: the criteria params bound only vout_1ms (0.62-0.65 V) while vout_5ms carries null min/max, and the deck's .meas for vout_5ms has no limits, so the acceptance test constrains only tau at one point and would pass compensating R/C substitutions. This exactly matches the declared limitations (ideal unloaded step response only) and the fixture requirement, which defines only the 1 ms window, so no declared criterion is violated and no requirement may be invented to escalate it. The suggestion to bound vout_5ms is a methodology improvement, properly recorded as info.
